findings.text: project_graph_uri() now returns only resolve_neo4j(auto_tunnel=False).uri, which by construction is always bolt://localhost:<port> (imas_codex/graph/profiles.py:452); on this cluster that is not the project graph, whose SLURM-discovered address is bolt://98dci4-gpu-0002:7687 (squeue: codex-neo4j RUNNING on 98dci4-gpu-0002) and where nothing listens on localhost:7687. Measured at 7351413cb: refuse_project_graph('bolt://98dci4-gpu-0002:7687') returns without refusing while refuse_project_graph('bolt://localhost:7687') fails; the set refused at base 3d790d60 contained both spellings. Since the fixture sets NEO4J_URI to the supplied endpoint before its own profile check, that check compares the override with itself (measured: with NEO4J_URI=bolt://98dci4-gpu-0002:7687, resolve_neo4j(auto_tunnel=False) returns that same string), so nothing stops disposable_neo4j_uri reaching _wipe(uri) against the live graph. Restore the tunnel/SLURM-resolved address in the refused set and make the profile check independent of the endpoint it was handed.

The new test takes its input from project_graph_uri() and hands it back to the fixture whose guard compares against that same function, so the two sides move together: the assertion holds for whatever address the function returns and cannot detect that the address is wrong. That is exactly the regression this commit introduced, and the test stayed green through all six runs it was exercised in. Assert against an independent source of the project graph's address (the SLURM-discovered service URL, as the base arm's a5 control used) and add an arm at bolt://98dci4-gpu-0002:7687 that must be refused.

The same refuse_project_graph('bolt://127.0.0.1:1') call is made twice in a row (lines 461 and 463); the second observes nothing the first did not, and the duplication suggests a distinct positive control was intended and lost.

The page states the removed-guard arm failed with 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE'; the log it cites, logs/negative-control-guard-removed.log, records neo4j.exceptions.ServiceUnavailable at conftest.py:452 _wipe ('Couldn't connect to localhost:7687'), and no log in the run contains 'DID NOT RAISE'. The conclusion that the test reddens holds, but the stated mechanism is contradicted by its own evidence, and the same claim is repeated in manifest.md:20.

item_verdicts.call_sites: The landed change is test-only, so no production module imports it; the production boundaries it drives are imas_codex/graph/profiles.py:resolve_neo4j and imas_codex/standard_names/dd_resolutions.py:dd_resolution_graph_reader, neither of which the diff modifies.
